claims.text: A deep neural-network interatomic potential can describe multicomponent high-entropy materials in both solid and liquid states near melting.
The DNN reference would be trained on ab initio liquid configurations of multicomponent HEAs near their melting points.
A DNN potential will capture the configurational diversity of an HEA liquid better than a conventional EAM reference.
Replacing an EAM reference with the DNN potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with the DNN potential will measurably reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method applies to multicomponent refractory HEAs containing elements such as Hf, Ta, Zr, Ti, and Nb in solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The DNN potential should be used as the reference potential during thermodynamic integration in place of a traditional EAM potential.
The applicable temperature interval is approximately 0.9 Tm to Tm.
Multicomponent mixing produces extensive configurational diversity in refractory HEA liquids over approximately 0.9 Tm to Tm.
A DNN's many-body representation can accurately map the complex ab initio energy landscape of a dense multicomponent liquid onto a classical potential.
EAM potentials have simpler functional forms than DNN potentials.
The functional form of EAM potentials prevents them from adequately representing the many atomic configurations in an ab initio liquid of a complex alloy.
A DNN trained to reproduce ab initio data captures subtle many-body interactions and variations in local atomic environments.
Improved representation of many-body interactions and local environments produces greater reference–target phase-space overlap.
Greater phase-space overlap yields a shorter and less mismatched thermodynamic-integration path.
DNN-referenced thermodynamic integration will produce lower free-energy error margins and a more continuous, accurate free-energy profile than TOR-TILD's EAM-referenced integration.
Current TOR-TILD EAM references suffer significant free-energy integration-path mismatch because they do not sample the full configurational space of the ab initio liquid.
The intervention may be less advantageous for systems with extremely directional bonding or insufficient ab initio training data.
The benefits of the DNN reference may diminish outside the 0.9 Tm to Tm regime.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction is system-dependent and cannot be specified without systematic validation.
